reasoning_traces.think:
The three primitives—EPA per dropback, YAC, and explosive plays—form a triadic kernel for evaluating offensive performance. EPA per dropback quantifies quarterback efficiency, YAC captures receiver impact post-catch, and explosive plays measure high-leverage outcomes. These metrics are interdependent: a high EPA QB may rely on receivers with high YAC to sustain drives, while explosive plays often result from both. The failure mode occurs when one metric is inflated without supporting others, e.g., a QB with high EPA but low YAC indicates poor receiver support. Dualities emerge in that EPA can be decomposed into components like YAC and explosive plays, forming a hierarchical structure for predictive modeling. The stochastic nature of these metrics necessitates Bayesian treatment in GSI for uncertainty quantification.
